claims.claim_text: No country has complete transparency, but several have gone far enough to prove the pieces work.
claims.evidence_quote: No country has achieved anything close to complete transparency, but several have gone far enough to prove it works.
claims.reasoning: Loglog mirrors source claim about incomplete transparency and proof of concept.

claims.claim_text: Sweden's 1766 Freedom of the Press Act was the world's first freedom of information law.
claims.evidence_quote: In 1766, Sweden passed the Freedom of the Press Act - the world's first freedom of information law.
claims.reasoning: Date and superlative match source exactly.

claims.claim_text: It abolished censorship, granted citizens access to government documents, and is now part of the constitution.
claims.evidence_quote: It abolished censorship and granted citizens the right to access government documents. It's now part of the Swedish constitution.
claims.reasoning: All three elements restate source without changing meaning.

claims.claim_text: Born from political conflict, not idealism: the Hats had held power for decades, the Caps saw accountability needed visibility.
claims.evidence_quote: This wasn't born from idealism. It was born from political conflict. The aristocratic "Hats" party had held power for decades, and the opposition "Caps" saw that accountability required visibility.
claims.reasoning: Negation and both party roles preserved faithfully.

claims.claim_text: Anders Chydenius drove the legislation through parliament, motivated explicitly by anti-corruption.
claims.evidence_quote: Anders Chydenius, a Finnish-Swedish priest and politician, drove the legislation through parliament. The motivation was explicitly anti-corruption.
claims.reasoning: Name and motivation attribution match source.

claims.claim_text: Two hundred and sixty years later Sweden still operates under offentlighetsprincipen, documents public by default.
claims.evidence_quote: Two hundred and sixty years later, Sweden still operates under this principle. It's called offentlighetsprincipen - the principle of public access. Government documents are public by default.
claims.reasoning: Time span, term, and default-public rule all match.

claims.claim_text: Sweden has not collapsed; Nordic countries consistently rank among the least corrupt and most effective democracies.
claims.evidence_quote: The country has not collapsed. Its government functions. In fact, Nordic countries consistently rank among the least corrupt and most effective democracies in the world.
claims.reasoning: Negation and Nordic ranking claim restated faithfully.

claims.claim_text: Seoul's 1999 OPEN system tracks 70 municipal tasks most prone to corruption.
claims.evidence_quote: In 1999, Seoul launched the OPEN system... It tracks 70 municipal tasks most prone to corruption
claims.reasoning: Year and count of 70 tasks match source.

claims.claim_text: It shows citizens exactly who made what decision, at which point in the process, in real time.
claims.evidence_quote: shows citizens exactly who made what decision, at which point in the process, in real time.
claims.reasoning: Verbatim restatement of source.

claims.claim_text: Before OPEN, applicants could not see how permits were processed, enabling bribery that could not be proven.
claims.evidence_quote: Before OPEN, applicants for government permits couldn't see how their applications were processed. This opacity enabled bribery... and nobody could prove it.
claims.reasoning: Opacity-causes-bribery and unprovability both preserved.

claims.claim_text: Research confirmed corruption decreases as e-participation increases; the UN, OECD, and World Bank recognized it.
claims.evidence_quote: Research confirmed... "corruption decreases as e-participation increases." The system was recognized by the UN, OECD, and World Bank.
claims.reasoning: Finding and three recognizing bodies match source.

claims.claim_text: Estonia's X-Road is a distributed data exchange layer connecting 929+ institutions, 1,887 information systems, 3,000+ services.
claims.evidence_quote: It's a distributed data exchange layer connecting 929+ institutions, 1,887 information systems, and 3,000+ digital services.
claims.reasoning: All three counts and description match source exactly.

claims.claim_text: Every transaction is timestamped and cryptographically signed, and all data access is logged.
claims.evidence_quote: Every transaction is timestamped and cryptographically signed. All data access is logged.
claims.reasoning: Both assertions restated without change.

claims.claim_text: Citizens can see who accessed their data and why.
claims.evidence_quote: Citizens can see who accessed their data and why.
claims.reasoning: Verbatim match.

claims.claim_text: Estonia ranks 2nd in the UN E-Government Development Index with no major breaches in over 20 years despite constant cyber attacks.
claims.evidence_quote: Estonia now ranks 2nd in the UN E-Government Development Index... no major security breaches in over 20 years, despite constant cyber attacks.
claims.reasoning: Ranking, breach claim, and time span match source.

claims.claim_text: X-Road is open source under an MIT license and deployed in 20+ countries.
claims.evidence_quote: It's open source (MIT license) and deployed in 20+ countries.
claims.reasoning: License and deployment count faithful.

claims.claim_text: X-Road proves the infrastructure is technically feasible; the technology is not the bottleneck, the will is.
claims.evidence_quote: X-Road proves the "every email available up the chain" infrastructure is technically feasible. The technology is not the bottleneck. The will is.
claims.reasoning: Conclusion and not-the-bottleneck negation preserved.

claims.claim_text: Brazil's 2004 Transparency Portal publishes all federal spending: contracts, transfers, salaries, travel expenses, government credit card transactions.
claims.evidence_quote: ### Brazil: Following the Money (2004)... publishes all federal spending: contracts, transfers, salaries, travel expenses, and government credit card transactions.
claims.reasoning: Year from heading and all five categories match source.

claims.claim_text: The portal receives over 20 million accesses per year.
claims.evidence_quote: It receives over 20 million accesses per year.
claims.reasoning: Figure matches source exactly.

claims.claim_text: The Transparency Card sends real-time notifications: over 430,000 active cards, 20+ million notifications sent.
claims.evidence_quote: sends real-time notifications to citizens about political spending - over 430,000 active cards, 20+ million notifications sent.
claims.reasoning: Both counts and real-time detail match source.

claims.claim_text: Journalists used the Access to Information Law to uncover 60GB of hidden pension data going back 27 years.
claims.evidence_quote: When journalists used Brazil's Access to Information Law to investigate, they uncovered 60GB of hidden pension payment data going back 27 years.
claims.reasoning: Law, 60GB, and 27 years all match source.

claims.claim_text: This is what happens when citizens get CEO tools: they find the fraud.
claims.evidence_quote: This is what happens when you give citizens the tools to be CEOs: they find the fraud.
claims.reasoning: Paraphrase preserves the same meaning.

claims.claim_text: Since 2019 New Zealand publishes all Cabinet papers and minutes within 30 business days of decisions.
claims.evidence_quote: Since 2019, New Zealand has proactively published all Cabinet papers and minutes online within 30 business days of decisions being made.
claims.reasoning: Year and 30 business day window match source.

claims.claim_text: Cabinet deliberations are typically the most protected category of government information anywhere.
claims.evidence_quote: cabinet deliberations are typically the most protected category of government information anywhere in the world.
claims.reasoning: Qualifier typically and superlative both retained.

claims.claim_text: The government has not ground to a halt; ministers still deliberate, but citizens can see why decisions were made.
claims.evidence_quote: The government has not ground to a halt. Ministers have not stopped deliberating. What has changed is that citizens can see why their government made the decisions it made.
claims.reasoning: Negations and changed-visibility claim preserved.

claims.claim_text: Taiwan's vTaiwan uses Pol.is: citizens vote agree or disagree, no replies allowed, and consensus statements surface.
claims.evidence_quote: Taiwan's vTaiwan platform uses Pol.is... others vote agree or disagree (no replies allowed... and an algorithm surfaces statements that find cross-group consensus rather than divisive ones.
claims.reasoning: All mechanics including no-replies negation match source.

claims.claim_text: By 2018, 26 issues had been processed and 80% led to government action.
claims.evidence_quote: By 2018, 26 issues had been processed, and 80% led to government action.
claims.reasoning: Year, count, and percentage match source exactly.

claims.claim_text: This is not core transparency but what becomes possible downstream of transparency.
claims.evidence_quote: This isn't core transparency - it's what becomes possible downstream of transparency.
claims.reasoning: Negation and downstream framing retained faithfully.
